label: Workday
description: Arcade.dev tools for interacting with Workday

tools.name: CreateTimeOffRequest
tools.description:
Request time off for the signed-in worker, asking for a draft by default.

Set mode to submit only when the worker asks for submission. Existing drafts must
be submitted in the Workday UI; existing requests must also be changed or cancelled
there. The receipt reports the confirmed state, or created_status_unknown when
read-back cannot confirm it. In that case, look up the request's status using the
returned identifiers; do not repeat the create. Recorded amounts appear in days;
requested_days preserves the values sent, and missing amounts are unconfirmed. The type's
rules are resolved from Workday first, so a reason, a position, and an omitted
quantity are checked against that type before anything is written. Workday owns the
rest of the validation; its rejections come back as errors describing what to change.

In the receipt, days[].date matches the requested date and days[].unit labels only
that entry's recorded amount. Missing quantity means unconfirmed, never zero.
requested_days contains the quantities (including defaults) and clock times sent.
status is draft_saved, submitted, approved, or sent_back when confirmed;
created_status_unknown means the request exists but its state is unknown, and
blocked_by_warning means nothing was written. requires_workday_ui_action=false
on an unconfirmed receipt means no action was established; read status before advising.

parameters.name: time_off_type_id
parameters.description: The Workday identifier of the time-off type being requested. Use a time_off_type_id from the worker's eligible time-off types; display names are not accepted. One type per request. The receipt echoes the selected type.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: One entry per unique date in YYYY-MM-DD format; date is the start date for clock-time requests. Dates need not be consecutive. quantity must be positive and counted in the selected type's unit: for an hourly type, 4 means four hours and 0.5 means half an hour, not half a day. Omit quantity only when the configured daily_default_quantity is positive; otherwise provide an explicit positive amount. start_time and end_time must be paired 24-hour HH:MM or HH:MM:SS times, passed unchanged with no time-zone conversion. Both are mandatory when the type requires them. An earlier end means the next date only when crossing_over_midnight_enabled is true; equal times are invalid.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Whether to submit the request for approval or leave it as an unfinished draft. Use submit only when the worker asks to send the request for approval. An existing draft must be submitted in the Workday UI. Defaults to draft.

parameters.name: reason_id
parameters.description: The Workday identifier of the reason for the time off. Defaults to an empty string, which sends no reason and suits a type that does not require one; when the type requires one, use one of that type's allowed reasons.

parameters.name: note
parameters.description: A short note stored on the request. Defaults to an empty string, which sends no note.

parameters.name: position_id
parameters.description: The Workday identifier of the position the time off is taken against. Defaults to an empty string, which uses the worker's only eligible position and suits types that are not scoped per position.

parameters.name: proceed_on_warning
parameters.description: Create the request even if Workday returns warning-level validations. Defaults to false, which reports the warnings and writes nothing.

output.description: What was created in Workday, or what blocked it

tools.name: ListEligibleTimeOffTypes
tools.description:
List the time-off types the signed-in worker can request, with their rules.

Each entry includes its display name and time_off_type_id. Retrieve the options here
and pass the chosen ID to the date check and request tools. Each entry also carries what
Workday reports for that type: a default quantity, whether a reason is mandatory
and which reasons are allowed, whether a position must be named, and whether clock
times are required, determine the quantity, or may cross midnight. `draft_support`
reports evidence of existing drafts. Requests use draft mode by default; set mode
to submit only when the worker asks for submission.

Each type's unit is the unit to use for request quantities; do not pass fractions
of a full day for an hourly type. start_and_end_time_required requires both clock
times. calculate_quantity_based_on_start_and_end_time means Workday determines the
recorded quantity from those times. crossing_over_midnight_enabled permits an
earlier end time on the following date, keeping the span under 24 hours.

parameters.name: effective_date
parameters.description: Return the types the worker is eligible for as of this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Eligibility varies by date, so use the first date being requested off. Defaults to an empty string, which uses today.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum types to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (the first result).

output.description: Time-off types the worker can request

tools.name: ListTimeOffBalances
tools.description:
Show how much time off the signed-in worker has left, by plan.

Balances come back exactly as Workday calculates them for the as-of date; this
tool never projects or totals an accrual Workday did not return. It reads the
signed-in worker record to address the balances to that worker. Read `coverage`
before relaying an empty list: it says whether no plan is tracked for this worker
or the read simply did not finish, and a worker whose time off is not
balance-tracked can still request time off.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Return only balances in this absence category. Defaults to every category Workday returns for the worker, including leave-of-absence balances.

parameters.name: effective_date
parameters.description: Report balances as of this date (YYYY-MM-DD). A future date returns what Workday projects for that date. Defaults to an empty string, which reports the balance as of today.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum balances to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (the first result).

tools.name: ListTimeOffRequests
tools.description:
List the signed-in worker's time-off requests and where each one stands.

Defaults to no date bound, subject to the read cap. Provide dates to narrow the
upstream search when results are incomplete. Requests come back in ascending order
of their earliest matching date. The first page contains the earliest matching
requests, which may be years in the past when no lower date bound is supplied.
For upcoming or next time off, set from_date to today's date in YYYY-MM-DD;
the unbounded first page does not identify the next time off. For time off already
taken, set to_date to today's date, and for a period such as this year, pass both
bounds.

A request with different types, units, statuses, positions, reasons, or notes
appears as separate groups sharing one request_id. All matching groups stay on
one page and count as one request. Dates and quantities describe only matching
entries within the requested window. Capped reads mark groups incomplete and omit
quantity totals. Each group reports its own status and action guidance. Existing
requests must be changed or cancelled in Workday; this toolkit cannot modify them.

requests[].dates are YYYY-MM-DD dates inside the selected window; out-of-window
days of the same request are excluded. Each group's unit applies only to that group.
result_count, total_count, limit, and offset count distinct request IDs, not groups.
Page with has_next_page and next_offset. results_truncated means the upstream read
was capped; no offset completes that read, so narrow the date bounds or check Workday.
requires_workday_ui_action identifies drafts or sent-back groups needing action;
use their workday_ui_action, falling back to the response's shared guidance.
status=unknown means Workday's status was missing or unrecognized. Check Workday
to confirm its state and any required action; requires_workday_ui_action=false
does not establish that no action is needed for an unknown status.

parameters.name: request_id
parameters.description: Only include the time-off request or day entry with this request_id or entry_id from an earlier result. An entry ID selects only that entry; an event ID selects its matching day entries, subject to other filters. Provide dates to narrow collection searches. A complete search with no match reports an error; a capped search reports that its results are incomplete. Defaults to an empty string, which selects all matching entries.

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Return only groups currently in these statuses. Use unknown to select entries whose Workday status was missing or unrecognized. Defaults to every status Workday reports, including past approved requests as well as outstanding requests.

parameters.name: time_off_type_id
parameters.description: Return only groups of the time-off type with this Workday identifier. Use a time_off_type_id from an earlier listing or eligible-type result; display names are not accepted. Each returned request echoes its own time-off type. Defaults to an empty string, which returns every type.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: Return day entries on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). For upcoming or next time off, resolve today to YYYY-MM-DD and pass it here. Defaults to an empty string, which sets no lower bound.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: Return day entries on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to an empty string, which sets no upper bound.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum requests to return (1-100). Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: 0-indexed starting position. Defaults to 0 (the first result).

output.description: Where the worker's time-off requests stand

tools.name: ValidateTimeOffDates
tools.description:
Check whether Workday accepts each date for the selected time-off type.

Send the candidate dates together before creating a request. Each result separates
date acceptance from the configured default and existing bookings. A default does
not establish a maximum, and a missing default says nothing about the worker's
schedule. Accepted dates therefore have unknown capacity; Workday validates the
requested quantity on submission.

Booking totals include only matching known units and position scope. Incompatible
units or ambiguous positions leave the total unknown. Worker-based checks include
bookings regardless of their position reference; position-scoped checks exclude
bookings against another position. Incomplete booking lookups omit all booked totals
and disclose that the booking names shown are partial results.

dates[].valid reports date acceptance, not available quantity. valid_count counts
accepted dates. bookable_spans stays empty because maximum capacity is unknown;
this does not mean none of the dates are valid. Read coverage_note for lookup limits.

parameters.name: time_off_type_id
parameters.description: The Workday identifier of the time-off type the dates are being checked for. Use a time_off_type_id from the worker's eligible time-off types; display names are not accepted. The response echoes the selected type.

parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: The calendar dates to check (YYYY-MM-DD each), at most 60 per call. Relative words such as tomorrow are not resolved; send resolved calendar dates.

parameters.name: position_id
parameters.description: The Workday identifier of the position the time off would be taken against. If several positions are eligible, provide one of their identifiers. Defaults to an empty string, which uses the worker's only eligible position and suits types that are not scoped per position.

output.description: Whether each requested date is valid

tools.name: WhoAmI
tools.description:
Identify the Workday worker the connection is signed in as, and their jobs.

Call this before acting on the worker's record so the answer is anchored to the
right person and tenant. Every other tool in this toolkit acts on this same worker
and cannot be pointed at anyone else.

output.description: The signed-in worker's identity and work context

summary:
Arcade toolkit for interacting with Workday on behalf of a signed-in worker. Enables reading worker identity, time-off balances, eligible time-off types, and existing requests, as well as validating dates and creating or submitting time-off requests.

## Capabilities

- **Worker identity:** Resolve the signed-in worker and their job(s) before taking any action; all tools operate on this same worker and cannot target another.
- **Time-off balances & eligibility:** Retrieve balance snapshots exactly as Workday calculates them, and list eligible time-off types with their rules (units, required reasons, position requirements, clock-time settings, draft support).
- **Date validation:** Check candidate dates against a selected time-off type before creating a request; results report acceptance per date and any known bookings, but not available quantity.
- **Request creation:** Draft or submit time-off requests with type-resolved rules; handles unknown confirmation states, warnings that block writes, and incomplete read-backs without repeating the create.
- **Request listing & status:** Page through existing requests with optional date bounds, grouped by type/unit/status/position; surfaces draft and sent-back requests that require action in the Workday UI.
- **UI handoff awareness:** Existing requests cannot be modified or cancelled via this toolkit; the tools explicitly signal when Workday UI action is required.

## OAuth

Uses OAuth 2.0 via the **Workday** provider. The signed-in user's identity determines which worker record all tools read and write.

## Secrets

- **`WORKDAY_BASE_URL`** — The base URL of your organization's Workday REST API endpoint (e.g., `https://wd2-impl-services1.workday.com`). This value is specific to your Workday environment and data center. Find it in your Workday tenant's API configuration or by consulting your Workday system administrator. It is also visible in the URL of your Workday tenant's web interface.

- **`WORKDAY_TENANT_NAME`** — The unique tenant identifier for your Workday instance (e.g., `mycompany_impl` or `mycompany`). This is the subdomain or path segment that identifies your organization's Workday environment. Your Workday administrator can provide this; it also appears in the URL when you log in to Workday (e.g., `https://impl.workday.com/<tenant_name>/...`).

Store secrets in the Arcade dashboard or via the secrets API. See the [Arcade secrets configuration guide](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets) and manage your secrets at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
